anuppatti:
anupatti, anuppatti

aṃsa:
1aṃsa
m. [S. aṃśa], share, portion, part; Abh 485; 1102; Sadd 567,.23; Spk I 305,.15 (~o ti koṭṭhāso vuccati); Mp III 248,.12; — ifc see atīt’- (sv acceti2), anāgat’- (sv agacchati), ek’-, paccuppann’-, paṭiviṃs’-, mett’-, sukk’-; — see also āsa5, ekaṃsika.

2aṃsa
m. [ts], the shoulder; Abh 264; 1102; Vin II 217,.19 (pattaṃ thavikāya pakkhipitvā ~e ālaggetvā); A I 61,.30 (ekena … ~ena mātaraṃ parihareyya; Mp II 121,.13 : ekasmiṃ aṃsakūṭe ṭhapetvā); Sn 609 (na gīvāya na ~ehi na udarena); Ja I 9,.18 (khāribhāraṃ ~e katvā); VI 562,13* (~ato); Ap 541,.17 (~ehi samadhārayuṃ); — ifc see antar’-, ek’-, puṭ’-; —          °-kāsāva,       n., a yellow shoulder-cloth; Vism 65,.22; —           °-kūṭa,       m.n. [aṃsa + kūṭa1], “shoulder-prominence”, the shoulder; Vin III 127,.4; Ja VI 562,25´; Ps III 378,.21 (dve ~āni); Spk III 244,.8 (dvinnaṃ ~ānaṃ antare); Dhp-a IV 136,.1; —           °-baddha,       m., a shoulder-strap; Vin II 143,18* (in uddāna: thavikā ~aṃ ca, Be, Ee so; Ce °-bandhakaṃ; Se °-vaddhaṃ ca); Ap 310,.16 (~e jine datvā, Be, Ee so; Ce °-bandhe; Se °-vaddhe); —           °-baddhaka (and     °-bandhaka),       m., a shoulder-strap; Vin I 204,.9 (~o, Be so; Ce °-vaṭṭako; Ee °-bandhako; Se °-vaddhako) ≠ II 114,.7 (Be so; Ce °-bandhako; Ee, Se °-vaddhako); Vv 33:215 (~aṃ, Be so; Se °-bandhakaṃ; Ce, Ee °-vaṭṭakaṃ); Sp 350,.25 (~ena, Be so; Ce, Se °-vaddhakena; Ee °-vaṭṭakena); —            °-bandhana,       n., a shoulder-strap; It-a II 67,.33 (~aṃ, eds so) = Sv 528,.17 (Be °-baddhakaṃ; Ce, Ee °-vaṭṭakaṃ; Se °-vaddhakaṃ); —           °-vaṭṭaka (and     °-vaddhaka),       m., a shoulder-strap; Vin I 204,.9 (~o, Ce so; Be °-baddhako; Ee °-bandhako; Se °-vaddhako) ≠ II 114,.7 (Ee, Se °-vaddhako; Be °-baddhako; Ce °-bandhako); Vv 33:215 (~aṃ, Ce, Ee so; Be °-baddhakaṃ; Se °-bandhakaṃ); Sp 350,.25 (~ena, Ee so; Be °-baddhakena; Ce, Se °-vaddhakena); Vin-vn 859 (~e).

3aṃsa
m. [S. -aśra], point, corner; edge, facet (frequently in combination with numerals); Vv 64:2 (phalehi ~ehi atīva saṅgatā; Vv-a 275,.25 : ~ehī ti kubbaraphale patiṭṭhitehi heṭṭhima-aṃsehi); As 317,.23 (catūhi ~ehi yuttaṃ caturaṃsaṃ); Vv-a 304,.1; — ifc see aṭṭh’- (sv aṭṭha2), āyat’- (sv āyamati), catu-r-, cūḷ’- (sv culla1), cha-ḷ- (sv cha2), ti-y-, soḷas’-; — see also aṃsi, assa2.
chamā:

Ja V 406,9* (~ī pupphavicitrasanthatā; 406,31´ : bhūmiyaṃ patthaṭā piṭṭhipāsāṇā, Ce, Ee so; Be bhūmi-samapatthaṭā; Se bhūmisamamatthakā).

2chamā
f. [S. kṣamā; or perhaps Pāḷi rather formed from chamā1], the earth; Abh 181 (vasundharā ~ā bhūmi); Sadd 412,.14 (~ā ti paṭhavī); — acc. chamaṃ (or for chamā1?), on the ground; to the ground; Thī 494 (disvāna ~aṃ nisinne; Thī-a 262,.22 : ~an ti chamāyaṃ); 514 (kese va ~aṃ khipi Sumedhā); Ja VI 89,18´ (chamā ti ~āya paṭhaviyan ti attho, ~an ti pi pāṭho, paṭhaviṃ patitaṃ viyā ti attho); — loc. chamāya(ṃ), on the ground; on to the ground; Vin I 286,.22 (bhikkhū ~āya cīvaraṃ pattharanti); M III 164,.25 (bālaṃ … ~āya vā semānaṃ); Sn 401 (mañce ~āyaṃ va sayetha santhate); Pv 40:3 (paripatāmi ~āyaṃ); Thī 88 (~āya seyyaṃ kappemi); Ja VI 195,19* (~āyaṃ ce nisiñcissaṃ); Mil 101,.2 (patamāne pi ~āyaṃ candimasuriye); Dhp-a III 273,.15 (~āya nisinnā suttaṃ kantati); —      °-nikiṇṇa,   mfn., strewn on the ground; D III 6,.9 (Korakkhattiyo kukkuravatiko catukuṇḍiko ~aṃ bhakkhasaṃ mukhen’ eva khādati, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee °-nikkiṇṇaṃ; or perhaps chamā1 and not a cpd); —       °-nikkhitta,   mfn., thrown down on the ground; M I 387,.19 (Seniyo kukkuravatiko dukkarakārako ~aṃ bhuñjati, Ce, Ee so; Be ~aṃ bhojanaṃ; Se chamāyaṃ nikkhittaṃ bhojanaṃ; or perhaps chamā1 and not a cpd); — see also khamā1.
dussa:
1dussa
n. (and m.?) [cf S. dūrśa, dūṣya; BHS duṣya], cloth; clothes; Abh 290 (~aṃ coḷo ca sāṭako); Vin II 128,.23 (akkamatu bhante bhagavā ~āni akkamatu sugato ~āni yaṃ mama assa dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāyā ti); III 56,.17 (mahagghaṃ ~aṃ passitvā); V 172,.14 (iminā ~ena kaṭhinaṃ attharissāmī ti); D II 164,.13 (tesaṃ ca pañcannaṃ °-yugasatānaṃ dve va ~āni na ḍayhiṃsu yaṃ ca sabba-abbhantarimaṃ yaṃ ca bāhiraṃ, Be, Ce so; Ee, Se omit na); M II 92,.8 (Kokanadaṃ ca pāsādaṃ odātehi ~ehi santharāpetvā); 155,.7 (isi kesamassuṃ kappetvā mañjeṭṭhavaṇṇāni ~āni nivāsetvā); Pv 10:3 (hand’ uttarīyaṃ dadāmi te imaṃ ~aṃ nivāsaya); Ja I 60,.12 (sīsaṃ khuddakaṃ ~āni bahūni); V 434,.7 (~aṃ muñcati ~aṃ bandhati); VI 185,.10 (bodhisattaṃ … naṅguṭṭhe gahetvā ~aṃ pothento viya pothesi); Ap 2,.27 (kapparukkhā bahū atthi … sabbaṃ ~aṃ samāhantvā acchādemi ticīvaraṃ); 185,.6 (buddhassa gacchamānassa ~ā dhāvanti pacchato); 380,.17 foll. (pāduddhare pāduddhare ~aṃ nibbattate mama heṭṭhā ~amhi tiṭṭhāmi); Mil 309,.21 (gandhaṃ vā mālaṃ vā ~aṃ vā aññataraṃ vā kiñci adhiṭṭhahitvā cetiye ukkhipati); Ap-a 367,.26 (cīnapaṭṭasomārapaṭṭādike ~e laggetvā); — ifc see kaṭhina- (sv kaṭhina2), cīvara-, chava-; —      °’-anta,   m. [dussa + anta1], the end of the cloth; a cloth, a screen; Ja I 467,.19 (palāpatumbaṃ ~e bandhitvā, Be, Se so; Ce, Ee dasante); Vism 312,.17 (~e baddhena ekakahāpaṇen’ eva, Be so; Se bandhena; Ce dasante; Ee dusante bandhena); Sp 696,.9 (~e baddhakahāpaṇādīhi yeva saddhiṃ coḷakāni denti, Be, Se so; Ce, Ee dasante); Dhp-a I 180,.8 (paṇṇaṃ tassa ~e bandhi, Be, Se so; Ce, Ee dasante); — ifc see tiro-; —       °-kuṭi,   f., a tent;? Sp 745,.21; Vin-vn 916; —       °-cālanī,   f., a cloth sieve; Vin I 202,.31; —       °-paṭa,   m., a cloth screen; S II 102,.1 (cittakaro … bhittiyā vā ~e vā itthirūpaṃ … abhinimmineyya, Ce, Se so; Be, Ee °-paṭṭe); —       °-paṭṭa,   m., a strip of cloth; Vin II 266,.10 (bhikkhuniyo … ~ena pāsuke namenti dussaveṇiyā … dussavaṭṭiyā …; Sp 1293,.12 : ~enā ti setavatthapaṭṭena); Ps I 56,.13 (ghanaputhulena ~ena mukhabandhanaṃ katvā, Be, Ce, Ee so; Se °-paṭena); Pj II 111,.22 (~ena sīsaṃ veṭhetvā); Vin-vn 2955; —       °-pallaṭṭhikā,   f., a posture held with the help of a cloth (see H. Lüders, 1941, p. 5; A.K. Coomaraswamy, 1956, fig. 202); Vin IV 189,.30 (hatthapallatthikāya vā ~āya vā antaraghare nisīdati; Sp 891,.31 : ettha āyogapallatthikā pi ~ā yeva); Vism 79,.2 (ukkaṭṭhassa n’ eva apassenaṃ na ~ā na āyogapaṭṭo vaṭṭati); Sv 1034,.30 (~aṃ vā hatthapallatthikaṃ vā karoti); Vin-vn 1892; —       °-pothima,  poṭhima,   n. (?), (like a) beating of cloth; Ja IV 457,.25 (tantamajjitaṃ nāma majji naṅguṭṭhe gahetvā ~aṃ nāma poṭhesi, Be, Se so; Ce, Ee °-poṭhimaṃ poṭhesi; = Cp-a 128,.18 : Be, Se °-pothanaṃ; Ce, Ee °-poṭhanaṃ); —       °-vaṭṭi,   f., a roll of cloth; Vin II 266,.11 (bhikkhuniyo … ~iyā pāsuke namenti); Vin-vn 2955; —       °-veṇi,   f., a twist or plait of cloth; Vin II 266,.11; Sp 1293,.13 (~iyā ti dussena kataveṇiyā); Vin-vn 2955.

2dussa
[according to ct = amussa, sg. m. gen. of asu2 qv]; of that; Ja III 54,1* (dussa me khettapālassa rattibhattaṃ apābhataṃ; 54,4´ : yo esa mamāvidūre khettapālo vasati dussa amusssā ti atthi, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee wr asammussā ti) quoted Cp-a 105,29* (Be, Se so; Ce, Ee assa; 105,.34 : ~ā ti amussa, Be, Se so; Ce, Ee assā ti) and Sadd 278,.8; cf Sadd 277,.30 (amusaddassa nāmikapadamālā vuccate asu amu … amussa dussa); 632,.24 (gāthāsu chandamabhedatthaṃ akkharalopo: adussa mama khettapālassa dussa me khettapālassa).
eva:
1eva
ind. [ts], (after ṃ and vowels usually taking the form yeva qv; after long vowels also taking the form va2 qv), a particle emphasising the word it follows; Abh 1152 (evāvadhāraṇe); Sadd 896,.1 (eva iti avaṭṭhānatthe); 902,.22 foll.; — 1. that very …, the same …; exactly that …; just …; Vin III 160,.4 (āyasmā Dabbo … aṅguliyā jalamānāya purato purato gacchati te pi ten’ eva ālokena … piṭṭhito piṭṭhito gacchanti); D I 90,.19 (yāy’ eva kho pan’ atthāya … tam eva atthaṃ …); 94,.24 (etth’ eva te sattadhā muddhā phalissati); S I 46,.18 (tatth’ ev’ antaradhāyī ti); 58,4* (ye naṃ dadanti saddhāya … tam eva annaṃ bhajati); A I 142,.12 (yad eva me sāmaṃ ñātaṃ … tad evāhaṃ vadāmī ti); Dhp 344 (mutto bandhanam eva dhāvati); Ja VI 331,.3 (mahāsatto … raññā supinadiṭṭhavelāyam eva … paṭisandhiṃ gaṇhi); 346,.13 (taṃ divasam eva); Vism 172,.25 (sesaṃ vuttanayen’ eva veditabban ti); Sp 292,.20 (es’ eva nayo kuñcikakosake pi); Spk I 123,.15 (yasmiṃ yasmiṃ iriyāpathe uppannaṃ tattha tatth’ eva niggaṇhāti); Mhv 5:200 (ajj’ eva pabbajissāma); — often with pronouns : Ja II 113,.9 (nāgarājā Sāriputto ahosi samuddadevatā aham evā ti); VI 364,.2 (sayam eva tāva upadhāremī ti); — 2. only, merely, just; M I 126,.14 (tāvad eva … yāva na …); S I 56,27* (sabbhir eva samāsetha); Sn 452 (piyavācam eva bhāseyya); 832 (idam eva saccan ti ca vādiyanti); Ja II 66,.25 (na bhikkhave idān’ eva Kokāliko naditvā pākaṭo jāto, pubbe pi …); VI 361,.9 (idhalokamattam eva oloketi na paralokaṃ); 366,.17 (ekāhen’ eva); Mil 18,.10 (eken’ eva uddesena); Vism 498,.20 (atthato ekam eva nibbānaṃ); 508,.33 (pattabbam eva h’ etaṃ maggena na uppādetabbaṃ); 513,1* (dukkham eva hi na koci dukkhito); Sp 290,.24 (sabbaṃ na vaṭṭati catukoṇam eva vaṭṭati); Spk II 250,.7 (ovādo ti vā anusāsanī ti vā atthato ekam eva); Pj II 503,.13 (dvayā eva dvayatā); — 3. indeed, really; certainly; absolutely; even, still; D I 110,.9 (suddhaṃ vatthaṃ … sammad eva rajanaṃ paṭigaṇheyya); 222,.7 (tumh’ ev’ etaṃ dukkaṭaṃ); S I 57,13* (caranti bālā dummedhā amitten’ eva attanā); Dhp 32 (nibbānass’ eva santike); 338 (chinno pi rukkho punar eva rūhati); 402 (yo dukkhassa pajānāti idh’ eva khayam attano); Ja VI 336,18´ (āhū ti āha katheti ayam eva vā pāṭho); 374,.9 (mattikamakkhiten’ eva sarīrena); Spk I 108,.6 (vataṃ saṅkiliṭṭham eva); Dhp-a I 6,.25 (sakkā gehaṃ ajjhāvasanteh’ eva puññāni kātuṃ); 192,.7 (yaṃ kiñci katvā gaṇhissām’ evā ti); Pj I 166,.25 (sabbe ti anavasesā evā ti avadhāraṇe ekaṃ pi anapanetvā ti adhippāyo); — 4. eva is especially common in combination with other particles, eg : c’ eva … ca …, both … and …; Vin III 160,.15 (bhikkhū navakā c’ eva honti appapuññā ca); D I 91,.15 (sambahulā Sakyā c’ eva Sakyakumārā ca); A I 151,.15 (yo c’ eva dhammaṃ deseti yo ca dhammaṃ suṇāti); Ja V 198,11´ (vaṇo khajjati c’ eva kaṇḍuṃ ca karoti); Mil 86,.18 (ime dhammā nānatthā c’ eva nānāvyañjanā ca); Vism 443,.13 (sīlavisuddhi c’ eva cittavisuddhi cā ti); — n’ eva … na …, n’ eva … no …, neither … nor …; D I 96,.10 (n’ eva asakkhi muñcituṃ no paṭisaṃharituṃ); S I 54,.18 (n’ eva nandasi na ca socasī ti); Dhp 105 (n’ eva devo na gandhabbo); Ja VI 211,3* (n’ eva migā na ppasu no pi gāvo); Mil 145,.17 (n’ eva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maranā ti); Vism 451,.12 (n’ eva kammajam nākammajaṃ); — tath’ eva, just so, exactly so; Vin III 2,.5 (tayidaṃ bho Gotama tath’ eva); S I 61,15* (yathā petā tath’ eva te); A I 152,29* (yathā pi … tath’ eva); Ja VI 196,.17 (bodhisatto … Sakkadevarājalīḷāya ṭhito, Sudassano pi Accimukhī pi tath’ eva aṭṭhaṃsu); Mil 180,.2 (yathā ca … tath’ eva …); Vism 308,.18 (yathā … tath’ eva …); — kocid eva etc, someone or other; some or other; Vin III 160,.35 (gahapati ārāmaṃ agamāsi kenacid eva karaṇīyena); D I 103,.31 (kañcid eva mantanaṃ manteyya); M I 124,.30 (kocid eva puriso); Ja IV 402,.12 (kocid eva yācako); Vism 27,.28 foll. (yathā hi muggesu paccamānesu kocid eva na paccati avasesā paccanti evaṃ yassa puggalassa vacane kiñcid eva saccaṃ hoti sesaṃ alikaṃ ayaṃ puggalo muggasūpo ti vuccati); — evam eva, just so, just like that; D I 95,.24 (evam eva me bho Gotama sutaṃ yath’ eva bhavaṃ Gotamo āha); Mil 33,.30 (yathā … evam eva kho …); Sp 404,.21 (evam eva kho ti opammasampaṭipādanaṃ etaṃ); — with other particles eva seems to add little to the sense, and is untranslatable; Vin III 163,.22 (app eva nāma naṃ imamhā brahmacariyā cāveyyan ti); Th 869 (itv eva); Ja III 302,2* (vilapi tv eva so dijo); Sp 286,.11 (tassa Isigili tv eva samaññā udapādi); — 5. eva iic sometimes has the sense of evaṃ qv; — see evadassi(n), evarūpa, evācāra; — see also iva2.

2eva
ind. [= -īva < -i + iva1 qv], like, as; as it were; Dhp 149 (apatthāni alāpūn’ eva sārade); Ja VI 125,34* (ākiṇṇaṃ Indasadisehi vyaggheh’ eva surakkhitaṃ; 126,13´ : yathā nāma vyagghehi vā sīhehi vā …); 507,16* (saṇat’ eva brahāraññam; 507,27´ : nadati viya saṇantaṃ viya bhavissati, Be so; Ce nadatīva; Ee wr sannatantaṃ viya; Se nadati saddaṃ karoti viya); 576,6* (Rohiṇī h’ eva tambakkhī; 576,8´ : Rohiṇī viya); — see also ateva sv ati.

[khīra + udaka], milk and water; Ja II 104,.24 (tassa aṭṭhiṃ … ropāpetvā ~ena siñcāpesi); Mp I 234,.9; —       ° ôdakībhūta,   mfn. (perfectly mixed or compatible) like milk and water; Vin I 351,.18 (samaggā sammodamānā avivadamānā ~ā aññamaññaṃ piyacakkhūhi sampassantā viharathā ti) ≠ S IV 225,.12 ≠ A III 67,.4 (Mp III 271,.16 : ~ā ti khīrodakaṃ viya bhūtā ekībhāvaṃ upagatā); —       °’-odana,   m., rice and milk; rice cooked in milk; Vv 33:87 (~aṃ aham adāsiṃ); Ap 472,.8 (~aṃ adās’ aham); —       °-kākolī̆,   f., a root (yielding a milky juice) (of Fritillaria roylei?); Sp 834,.6 (in long cpd); m. (and n.) [S., BHS dharma], dhamma denotes (an interpretation of) the essential nature and reality of existence and experience, the way things are: it is descriptive and prescriptive; it denotes also an essential attribute of men or animals; a quality or characteristic; Abh 784 (~o sabhāve pariyattipaññāñāyesu saccappakatīsu puññe ñeyye guṇācārasamādhisū pi nissattatāpattisu kāraṇādo); see also Sv 99,.3 foll., Ps I 17,.16 foll., It-a I 37,.20 foll., Paṭis-a 18,.1 foll., Bv-a 13,.4 foll., As 38,.23 foll. and Sadd 560,.25 foll.; — for Buddhists dhamma is used to denote an interlocking and interdependent assembly of concepts: the true nature of the world of experience, how that world works, and the way to transcend it, as understood by the Buddha; the progressive stages of understanding and nibbāna ; the behaviour, the practice, required to achieve understanding of the way the world of experience works, ie the way to reach arhatship, nibbāna ; the understanding and practice taught by the Buddha, the substance of his teaching, the texts of the Canon, especially the Suttapiṭaka ; all constituents of the world of experience, physical and mental, external and internal, progressively more and more minutely analysed; all constituents of prescribed practice, appropriate and beneficial actions; prescriptions for the members of the saṅgha ; — for people generally dhamma is an interpretation of the essential nature of existence and experience; the way one should act, depending on who one is, to maintain the way things are and should be; duty; right; justice; normative and beneficial actions; — 1.
